report.source_text: Lumbar puncture demonstrated a normal opening pressure, elevated white blood cells (ranging from 85 to 501/mm3) with a lymphocytic predominance (87%), elevated red blood cells (ranging from 8 to 123/mm3), elevated protein (306 mg/dL), normal glucose and normal lactate dehydrogenase. Metabolic, neoplastic and preliminary autoimmune workup were negative, including oligoclonal bands, ACE, AQP4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG). Extensive infectious workup was negative (cerebral spinal fluid, CSF and serum), including MTB-QuantiFERON, MTB PCR, AFB, HIV, syphilis, coccidioides, histoplasma, cryptococcus, brucella, West Nile, Lyme disease and a meningitis/encephalitis panel (including HSV, cytomegalovirus and enterovirus).

report.source_text: Prior to discharge patient’s strength improved to 4/5 strength in the lower extremities. Given the association between GFAP astrocytopathy and malignancy, he was screened with CT chest-abdomen-pelvis and testicular ultrasound, which found no evidence of occult malignancy. He was discharged to a rehab facility on a steroid taper and mycophenolate mofetil.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 50s with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented with a 1-week prodrome of fever, nausea, vomiting, and generalized weakness, followed by acute neurological deterioration over 2 days with confusion, back pain, urinary hesitancy, and lower extremity numbness and weakness. On admission, he was febrile (38.9°C), disoriented, and demonstrated lower extremity weakness (4+/5 in hip and knee flexors) with hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral upgoing toes. MRI brain revealed diffuse leptomeningitis while thoracic and lumbar spine MRI were normal. CSF analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (85-501 WBC/mm³, 87% lymphocytes), elevated protein (306 mg/dL), and normal glucose. Extensive infectious workup (including MTB, HIV, syphilis, fungal, viral, Lyme, West Nile, and meningitis/encephalitis panel) and preliminary autoimmune markers (oligoclonal bands, ACE, AQP4, MOG) were negative. Empiric broad-spectrum antimicrobial coverage (vancomycin, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, acyclovir, fluconazole, RIPE, and dexamethasone) was initiated at admission. Several days later, the Mayo Clinic CSF autoimmune encephalitis panel returned positive for GFAP antibodies (1:128, reference <1:2), confirming GFAP-associated meningomyeloencephalitis. Antimicrobials were discontinued and the patient underwent five sessions of plasmapheresis. Prior to discharge, lower extremity strength improved to 4/5. Malignancy screening with CT chest-abdomen-pelvis and testicular ultrasound was negative. He was discharged to rehabilitation on a steroid taper and mycophenolate mofetil.
